ts.note: Edge receipt in microseconds. owa_event_raw.ts, and an input to the derived event id -- the resolution is what keeps two events of one session apart. Environmental so a request cannot set it and a queue drain cannot restamp it.

event_type.note: What happened. The tracker sends it and log.php also reads it with getRequestParam to call setEventType(), which sets a MEMBER -- getEventType() prefers that member and falls back to this property. Declared required:false with no default so the two cannot disagree: a default here would fabricate an event_type on events that carry their type on the member instead. It is already a column on the queue table, and v2 logs it on the fact row.

page_location.note: The complete page URL, query included, with nothing stripped. owa_event_raw.page_location, and the evidence the campaign tags are parsed out of -- page_url is the CANONICAL form and cannot answer that a second time. No callbacks on purpose: a filter here would defeat the column. A tracker cached before this shipped sends only page_url; Classes\Beacon\Compat renames it.

beacon_version.note: The tracker's BEACON FORMAT generation, sent on every beacon and stored on the row. Not a contract and not consulted at ingest: it is the evidence for deciding when a compat bridge can be deleted, which is otherwise a guess about how long a customer's cache policy lets an old tracker live. NULL means a tracker from before versioning -- generation 0 -- which is every tracker in the wild at the time this shipped.

event_seq.note: REQUEST scoped: the event's position in its session, counted on the device and stamped when the event is built. The cube sorts a session on this rather than on ts, because ts is edge receipt and a late beacon would otherwise sort after events that happened after it. Not required -- a tracker cached from before this sends nothing and the row keeps NULL, which the sort reads as 'no device order' rather than as position zero.

is_new_session_start.note: REQUEST scoped: rides exactly the one beacon that created the session, and is what SessionHandlers branches create-vs-update on.

is_new_visitor_created.note: REQUEST scoped: marks the one request that minted the visitor. Nothing consumes it yet -- it exists so v2 can raise first_visit from the request that actually created the visitor. Do not drop it as unused.

session_referer.note: Carried straight from the wire -- no callback, no default -- so it is on the event before the property pass starts. The old "must come after session_referer" comments on source/medium/search_terms described a constraint that never existed.

landing_url.note: The URL the session landed on, carried for the whole session so the server can resolve campaign tags from it on every beacon -- not just the first, where page_url would do. Replaces the six tagged_* params the tracker used to parse and re-send. Carried rather than derived because raw is the realtime surface: a value only a later pass produces does not exist for a live query. See resolveSource/taggedValue.

tagged_source.note: What the landing URL was tagged with. A claim, not a conclusion: the tracker lifts it off the URL and reports it. The server resolves the answer into the bare name in the server scope.

tagged_medium.note: What the landing URL was tagged with. A claim, not a conclusion: the tracker lifts it off the URL and reports it. The server resolves the answer into the bare name in the server scope.

Column type from base.commerce_transaction_fact, where the wire name differs from the column: ct_total is total_revenue, ct_country is billing_country. integer is the nearest type this vocabulary has to numeric: it applies $var + 0, so 12.50 stays 12.5 rather than truncating, and the handler rounds and converts to the stored value.

ct_line_items.note: Deliberately untyped. It arrives as a JSON string from the beacon but as an ARRAY when a PHP caller sets it directly, and cleanJson calls json_decode, which takes only a string. Declaring json here fataled every programmatic transaction. Enumerated so the wire surface is complete; coercion needs the polymorphism resolved first.

site_id.note: The tracked site. logEvent refuses an event naming a site this installation does not have. string, not integer: the integer type applies $var + 0, and these are 19-digit BIGINT ids where that risks precision. Nothing needs them arithmetically.

session_id.note: Minted by the tracker. string, not integer: the integer type applies $var + 0, and these are 19-digit BIGINT ids where that risks precision. Nothing needs them arithmetically.

visitor_id.note: Minted by the tracker and held in the v store. string, not integer: the integer type applies $var + 0, and these are 19-digit BIGINT ids where that risks precision. Nothing needs them arithmetically.

last_req.note: Timestamp of the previous request, on the CLIENT clock. It is subtracted from a server clock downstream, so it is not interchangeable with timestamp.

client_ts_usec.note: The client's own clock at send, microseconds. Subtracted from the server's receipt time into owa_event_raw.clock_offset_usec, so skew is a stored number rather than a silent error. NOT used as the event time: the server assigns that.

engagement_msec.note: Time accrued on the current page since the last report, in milliseconds. A DELTA, not a session total, so losing one beacon costs one increment rather than one page. Summed at read time; the engaged threshold is applied there too and never at collection.

content_group.note: Author-assigned grouping of pages. Page-scoped: set per page, so it cannot leak onto the next one.

consent_state.note: granted or denied, as the page declared it at send. Per event because it can change mid-session; absent stays absent, because no consent recorded is not the same as consent denied.

user_id.note: The site's OWN id for a logged-in person -- not user_name, which is a display name. The one field that outlives a cookie, and forward-only: events collected before someone identified themselves stay anonymous.

currency.note: ISO 4217, stored beside revenue. Without it a multi-currency store sums minor units of different things.

scroll_depth.note: Percentage of the document reached, on a scroll event. One event per threshold per page.

element_path.note: A CSS-ish path to the clicked element. dom_element_id is real on 0.09% of clicks and populated on 94%, so a path is what actually identifies what was clicked.

search_term.note: Site-search term, on a view_search_results event. Reaches reporting as the params.search_term path.

form_id.note: On form_start / form_submit. Both id and name are carried because either may be absent.
